title: Associations Between Self-Reported Previous Hepatitis C Diagnosis, Hepatitis C Treatment, and Current Binge Drinking Among Persons Who Inject Drugs-National HIV Behavioural Surveillance, 2015-2024.
abstract: Persons who inject drugs (PWID) are disproportionately affected by hepatitis C virus (HCV). Excessive alcohol use among PWID can lead to more rapid progression of liver disease among persons with HCV. We assessed associations between ever reporting HCV infection, ever reporting HCV treatment, and current binge drinking among PWID who participated in National HIV Behavioural Surveillance (NHBS) during 2015-2024. NHBS conducted biobehavioural surveys among PWID using respondent-driven sampling in 2015, 2018, 2022, and 2024. We estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) to assess the association between self-report of ever having HCV infection, HCV treatment, and binge drinking in the past 30 days. The percentage of PWID reporting binge drinking was 25.8% in 2015, 24.0% in 2018, 13.3% in 2022, and 17.2% in 2024. In adjusted analysis, we found a significant negative relationship between self-reported ever having HCV infection and binge drinking in the past 30 days in three of the four surveys: 2018 (aPR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.83-0.99), 2022 (aPR: 0.79, 95% CI:0.70-0.90), and 2024 (aPR:0.78, 95% CI: 0.65-0.93). We did not find significant associations between previously ever receiving treatment for HCV infection and binge drinking in the past 30 days across the four survey years. Among PWID, HCV infection was associated with reduced prevalence of binge drinking in 2018, 2022, and 2024. Our results support the importance of testing PWID for HCV infection and continued education on the harms associated with excessive alcohol use, including among persons who have received treatment for HCV infection.

title: Enhancing the Hepatitis C Cascade of Care: Implementation Science Approach in a Federally Qualified Health Center System.
abstract: Context Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a significant public health challenge in the United States, particularly among underserved populations. Despite curative treatments, systemic barriers often delay the care cascade. Program This quality improvement program aimed at improving the care of patients with chronic Hepatitis C within a Federally Qualified Health Center system in Southern California, known as AltaMed Health Services. The program involves AltaMed, serving more than 700 000 patients, primarily low-income people in underserved communities through an integrated delivery system for Latino and multiethnic individuals, focusing on enhancing screening and treatment processes for Hepatitis C. Methods A multipronged clinical workflow redesign was evaluated utilizing the RE-AIM framework to assess process and clinical between 2022 and 2024. Intervention included an electronic health record (EHR) Best Practice Advisory to identify patients due for HCV screening, a standardized direct-referral workflow, and a Linkage to Care team to manage prior authorization administrative tasks and patient outreach efforts. Evaluation Total descriptive HCV screening volumes increased from 30 212 to 47 951, with screening rates expanding from 3.4% to 7.3% in nonspecialty clinics. Treatment initiation rates shifted from 36% to 45%, and post-treatment patient outreach documentation changed from 48% to 73%. The average duration from diagnosis to treatment initiation was observed to be 55.9% lower, changing from 34 weeks in 2022 and 15 weeks in 2024. Discussion Establishing an Linkage to Care team, combined with automated EHR tools, can track alongside meaningful improvements in the safety-net HCV care cascade. Scaling models require careful consideration of specialized staffing and localized EHR infrastructure to advance health equity and global HCV elimination goals.

title: Focal Neurological Involvement in Adult-Onset Still Disease-Associated Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis: A Diagnostic Challenge
abstract: A woman in her late 40s with adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD), previously independent in mobility, personal care, and cognition, presented with fever, sore throat, and a diffuse erythematous eruption involving the palms, soles, and lower limbs. Her medical history was also significant for established hepatitis B infection, for which she had been receiving long-term entecavir therapy. Her regular immunomodulatory medications included anakinra 100 mg subcutaneously once daily and methotrexate 20 mg subcutaneously weekly, alongside folic acid; prednisolone had recently been discontinued. Anakinra and methotrexate were temporarily withheld for one week on rheumatology advice due to concerns regarding COVID-19 infection. Investigations revealed marked hyperferritinemia, with ferritin peaking at 23,321 μg/L, hypertriglyceridaemia, hypofibrinogenaemia, liver dysfunction and a peak HScore of 214, a diagnostic scoring system for reactive haemophagocytic syndrome supporting a diagnosis of haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), also termed macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) in the context of rheumatological disease. A SARS-CoV-2 reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) was positive; severe COVID-19 pneumonitis was considered a potential infectious trigger. The patient subsequently developed type 1 respiratory failure requiring admission to the intensive care unit (ICU). Despite treatment with corticosteroids and escalation of anakinra, her clinical course was complicated by profound encephalopathy, aphasia and focal neurological deficits. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated left temporoparietal restricted diffusion and superficial pial enhancement, while ophthalmological assessment identified a right homonymous hemianopia. Electroencephalography (EEG) demonstrated persistent left hemispheric dysfunction. Despite extensive infectious investigations identifying potential contributing pathogens, no single definitive trigger for HLH/MAS could be established. National multidisciplinary review considered a broad differential diagnosis for the neurological abnormalities, including central nervous system involvement secondary to HLH, peri-ictal changes, cerebral ischaemia, viral infection and occult intravascular lymphoma. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of HLH/MAS, in which multiple potential triggers and overlapping neurological manifestations may prevent identification of a single underlying aetiology despite extensive investigation. New-onset encephalopathy, aphasia, seizures or focal neurological deficits in patients with HLH/MAS should prompt early neurological assessment, appropriate MRI, EEG and cerebrospinal fluid investigations, and multidisciplinary specialist input. Neuroimaging findings should be interpreted alongside clinical, laboratory and other investigative findings, maintaining a broad differential diagnosis rather than prematurely attributing abnormalities to a single cause.

title: A universal molecular bridge unifying viral persistence and chronological tissue aging
abstract: Abstract Chronological aging and acute/post-acute viral infections (such as SARS-CoV-2 Orf7b, Epstein-Barr Virus, Hepatitis C Virus, and Long COVID extracellular vesicles [LC-EVs]) have traditionally been investigated as distinct pathological entities. Here, we establish a unifying mechanistic framework demonstrating that aging and chronic viral persistence converge on a common master regulatory network. Specifically, aging-induced fidelity loss of p53 and SIRT6, combined with viral upregulation of c-Myc and RUNX2, dismantles protective non-coding RNA brakes (miR-145) and longevity deacetylase pathways. We uncover a key feed-forward mechanism wherein hyperactivated RUNX2 directly activates and stabilizes c-Myc [14, 15]. Elevated c-Myc subsequently represses miR-145 while upregulating Tissue Factor (TF) and thrombin via lncRNA MEG3 induction [16], accelerating arterial thrombosis and microvascular occlusion. This dual transcriptional and epigenetic assault disinhibits tissue-destructive proteases like Granzyme K (GzmK), paralyzes the NRF2-Parkin-PGC-1α mitochondrial/peroxisomal axis, and drives structural remodeling and functional decline across multiple organs. Using stiff ordinary differential equation (ODE) modeling, we demonstrate that targeted host-directed restoration via p53/NRF2 co-activation and SIRT6-dependent pathways successfully re-establishes homeostatic control, clearing pathological effectors and rejuvenating tissue function.

title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Cholangiocarcinoma in Sulaymaniyah Governorate: A Population-Based Study
abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma is a rare highly malignant disease of the bile duct with a poor prognosis, and with a significant geographical variation in incidence, most of which are diagnosed as advanced, extrahepatic disease in older males. The study was to find out the incidence of cholangiocarcinoma in Sulaymaniyah Governorate. Identify its clinical and demographic profile; assess risk factors. The study was conducted in Sulaymaniyah Governorate (population of about 1.7 million) using all newly diagnosed cholangiocarcinoma cases of the population between May 2025 and May 2026, in a cross-sectional prospective study. Demographic, clinical and risk factor information was obtained for each case. Incidence rates were computed and descriptive analyses were carried out. There were 25 new cases of cholangiocarcinoma diagnosed. Most patients were male (72%) with a mean age of 70.2 years (range 58–89). There were 20% intrahepatic, and 80% of cases (70% perihilar, 30% distal) were extrahepatic. Most were at an advanced stage and had obstructive jaundice. Only 20% were surgical candidates, and 60% of these patients died within one year of diagnosis, while 80% were unresectable at diagnosis. Comorbidities included diabetes (40%), cirrhosis (20%), hepatitis B (16% locally), hepatitis C (4% locally), and smoking (32%) and obesity/metabolic syndrome (36%). In Sulaymaniyah, cholangiocarcinoma is a rare form of cancer. It mainly affects elderly men and most often presents as perihilar tumors, which are usually diagnosed at a late stage. Diabetes is the most common risk factor and hepatitis C is the least common risk factor.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Hepatitis C virus remodels lipid droplets to promote mitochondrial fatty acid accumulation and metabolic activation
abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatitis C virus (HCV) depends on host lipid metabolism and lipid droplets (LDs) for genome replication, assembly, and particle production, yet how LD structure and lipid utilization change over the course of infection remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the temporal remodeling of LD-associated metabolic pathways during HCV JFH-1 infection of human hepatoma Huh7 cells. HCV infection transiently increased LD fluorescence intensity at 24 h post-infection (hpi), followed by normalization or relative loss of LD signal at later time points. Concomitantly, LDs became progressively clustered and enlarged during late infection, despite reduced protein levels of the canonical LD fusion proteins CIDEA, CIDEB, and CIDEC, suggesting that HCV-induced LD enlargement is not associated with increased expression of CIDE proteins. Transcriptomic, RT-qPCR, and immunoblot analyses revealed time-dependent regulation of genes and proteins involved in LD structure, triglyceride synthesis, lipolysis, lipid uptake, and mitochondrial fatty acid utilization. Subcellular fractionation demonstrated preferential accumulation of fatty acids in mitochondrial fractions at 24–72 hpi. This redistribution was accompanied by increased oxygen consumption rate, elevated extracellular acidification, and progressive reactive oxygen species accumulation, indicating infection-associated metabolic activation and oxidative stress. Pharmacological inhibition of DGAT1-dependent LD biogenesis, LIPA-dependent lysosomal lipid hydrolysis, LIPE/HSL-dependent lipolysis, or CPT1-dependent mitochondrial fatty acid transport markedly reduced mitochondrial fatty acid accumulation and suppressed HCV-induced respiratory activity. Inhibition of LIPA or LIPE/HSL reduced both HCV RNA and core protein levels, whereas inhibition of CPT1 or DGAT1 had more pronounced effects on core protein than on viral RNA. Together, these findings support a model in which HCV dynamically remodels LDs, mobilizes LD-associated fatty acids, and redirects them toward mitochondria to support infection-associated metabolism and downstream stages of the viral life cycle. Lipid hydrolysis and mitochondrial fatty acid trafficking therefore represent potential host-directed targets for limiting HCV infection. IMPORTANCE Hepatitis C virus depends on host lipid metabolism for replication, assembly, and production of infectious particles, but how it uses lipid droplets over time remains incompletely understood. This study shows that hepatitis C virus dynamically remodels lipid droplets, causing an early increase in lipid storage followed by droplet enlargement and mobilization of fatty acids during later infection. The released fatty acids preferentially accumulate in mitochondria, where they are associated with increased cellular respiration and oxidative stress. Blocking lipid droplet formation, lipid breakdown, or fatty acid transport to mitochondria reduced this metabolic response and decreased viral RNA or core protein accumulation. Inhibition of lysosomal acid lipase and hormone-sensitive lipase suppressed both viral RNA and protein levels. These findings identify lipid droplet breakdown and mitochondrial fatty acid trafficking as important host processes used by hepatitis C virus and as potential targets for host-directed antiviral intervention.

title: Dupilumab in Children with Atopic Dermatitis and History of Liver Transplantation: Two Case Studies
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD), primarily diagnosed in children after orthotopic liver transplantation, is considered as potential transplant-acquired allergy (TAA) developed de novo due to long-term immunosuppressive therapy. The options for systemic AD therapy in this population are significantly limited as administration of cyclosporine A, methotrexate, systemic glucocorticoids, and Janus kinase inhibitors is associated with hepatotoxicity, potentiation of overall immunosuppression, and risk of latent viral infections reactivation. Dupilumab, monoclonal antibody to IL-4 receptor α-subunit, represents pathogenetically justified option due to selective blockade of Th2 signaling pathway while maintaining Th1-mediated immune response. Observations of two male patients aged 5 and 8 years with severe AD are presented. AD manifested 3–4 years after orthotopic liver transplantation performed in infancy for extrahepatic biliary atresia and congenital hepatic fibrosis. Reduction of skin lesions and itching severity, preservation of transplant function, and absence of any side effects were noted during the follow-up period. These observations demonstrate clinical efficacy and favorable safety profile of dupilumab in the management of severe AD in children with history of orthotopic liver transplantation (including those with concomitant chronic HBV infection) and confirm feasibility of its implementation in multidisciplinary management and regular monitoring of transplant function.

title: Frequency of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Patients with Non-Cirrhotic Liver: A Cross-Sectional Study of Liver Findings on Triphasic CT Scan
abstract: Background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) can arise in both cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic livers. In non-cirrhotic liver, diagnosis may be challenging because non-invasive imaging criteria have limitations, and histopathological confirmation may be required when guideline-based imaging criteria are not applicable. Triphasic CT provides multiphasic assessment of hepatic lesions and background liver morphology. Local data regarding HCC in patients without radiological cirrhosis are limited. This study aimed to determine the frequency of non-cirrhotic liver among patients with HCC evaluated by triphasic CT and compare selected clinical and radiological characteristics between cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic groups.Methodology: This cross-sectional study included 116 adults aged 18–70 years referred for triphasic CT evaluation of suspicious hepatic nodule(s). Patients were consecutively enrolled during the study period September 1st 2025 to March 1st 2026, from the referral population of Chughtai Lab, Lahore. No histopathological confirmation was reported in the submitted study dataset. Cirrhosis was classified radiologically using periportal space and caudate-to-right-lobe ratio measurements. Demographic, clinical, and CT variables were recorded and analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson chi-square tests.Results: Of 116 patients with HCC, 37 (31.9%) were classified as having non-cirrhotic and 79 (68.1%) as having cirrhotic liver morphology on triphasic CT. The mean age was 52.27 ± 10.50 years, and 86 (74.1%) patients were male. HCV infection was present in 52 (44.8%), HBV infection in 29 (25.0%), diabetes mellitus in 48 (41.4%), hypertension in 37 (31.9%), and smoking in 45 (38.8%). Mean lesion size was 4.94 ± 2.56 cm; 51 (44.0%) had lesions >5 cm and 82 (70.7%) had right-lobe involvement. No statistically significant associations were observed between radiological cirrhosis status and the assessed clinical or radiological variables (all p>0.05). Statistically significant differences in periportal space and caudate-to-right-lobe ratio measurements reflected the predefined radiological classification criteria for cirrhosis.Conclusion: Consideration of HCC in patients without radiological cirrhosis and careful multiphasic CT assessment is important, particularly when conventional imaging criteria for HCC diagnosis may not be applicable. Further studies with histopathological correlation and broader populations are warranted.

title: Delayed creatine kinase elevation after sonidegib therapy in a patient with decompensated cirrhosis and esophagogastric variceal hemorrhage: A case report
abstract: Sonidegib, a hedgehog pathway inhibitor targeting the smoothened receptor, is widely used in advanced basal cell carcinoma (BCC). Creatine kinase (CK) elevation is a recognized adverse event following treatment with sonidegib, but its safety in patients with decompensated cirrhosis remains unclear. The present study reports the case of a 77‐year‐old man with chronic hepatitis B‐related decompensated cirrhosis who developed CK elevation after sonidegib therapy for locally advanced BCC. The patient had received oral sonidegib at 200 mg/day for 35 days, which was discontinued due to worsening ascites. Shortly afterward, the patient experienced esophagogastric variceal hemorrhage and was admitted to the Department of Hepatology at Shuguang Hospital affiliated to Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (Shanghai China). At 4 days post‐admission (day 4) and 7 days after sonidegib discontinuation, CK was first found to be elevated to 3,291 U/l. The CK level peaked at 11,944 U/l on day 6, accompanied by elevated myoglobin, but without evidence of acute myocardial injury or renal impairment. Hypovolemia, electrolyte abnormality, critical disease‐associated myopathy, occult infection and concomitant medication were assessed as alternative or contributing explanations. A Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale score of 4 indicated a possible adverse drug reaction. The patient received intravenous fluid replacement, permanent withdrawal of sonidegib and close monitoring. The CK level returned to the reference range by day 21, and the myoglobin level normalized by day 57; both remained normal during the 3 months of follow‐up. This case is notable for the delayed severe CK elevation after sonidegib discontinuation in the combined setting of decompensated cirrhosis and acute variceal bleeding, and highlights the importance and need for close and extended CK monitoring, careful assessment of hepatic function, and individualized treatment decisions in patients with cirrhosis receiving sonidegib.

title: Knowledge and Awareness of Hepatitis Infections Among Pregnant Women Attending Antenatal Care in Tertiary Health Facilities in Ilorin Metropolis
abstract: Introduction: Hepatitis B and C infections remain important public health concerns during pregnancy because of their implications for maternal health and the risk of mother-to-child transmission. This study assessed awareness and knowledge of hepatitis infections among pregnant women attending antenatal care (ANC) in tertiary health facilities in Ilorin Metropolis, Kwara State, Nigeria. Methodology: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 400 pregnant women attending ANC in selected tertiary health facilities. Respondents were selected using multistage sampling. Data were collected using a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Associations between socio-demographic characteristics and knowledge were assessed using the chi-square test at p < 0.05. Results: Overall, 81.5% had heard of hepatitis, with Hepatitis B being the most recognized type (71.0%). Health workers were the major information source (69.0%), followed by radio/television (42.0%) and social media (33.0%). Overall, 67.0% had good knowledge, while 33.0% had poor knowledge. Knowledge was significantly associated with age, marital status, education, occupation, gestational age, and parity (p < 0.05). Conclusion: Awareness and knowledge were generally good, although gaps remained in transmission and prevention. Strengthening structured hepatitis education during ANC is recommended.

title: Inter-/Intra-Reader Variability in Ultrasound Measurement of Skin-to-Liver Capsule Distance and Hepato-Renal Index.
abstract: Background Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), if untreated, results in cirrhosis. Skin-to-liver capsule distance (SCD) and hepato-renal index (HRI) are ultrasound-derived biomarkers used in the quantitative assessment of hepatic steatosis, but manual measurements introduce operator variability. This study quantified inter- and intra-reader variability in SCD and HRI among patients with cirrhosis and assessed whether measurement precision differed by disease etiology. Methods A total of 1825 ultrasound examinations from 560 adults with cirrhosis were retrospectively identified. SCD and HRI reproducibility coefficients (RDC) were quantified between two independent readers; repeatability coefficients (RC) were quantified for repeated measurements by a single reader with a ≥28-d washout period. Precision was compared among MASLD, alcohol-related liver disease, metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-associated liver disease and chronic hepatitis C virus subgroups using one-way ANOVA with pairwise t-tests and false discovery rate (FDR) correction (p ≤ 0.05). Results A total of 1616 images were evaluable for SCD and 1065 for HRI. Median SCD was 21.2 mm and 20.8 mm; median HRI was 1.11 and 1.14, for Reader 1 and Reader 2, respectively. RDCs were 19.9% (SCD) and 55.8% (HRI) and RCs were 19.7% (SCD) and 52.2% (HRI). Neither SCD nor HRI reproducibility differed by etiology. HRI showed overall inter-reader variability differences (p = 0.023), but no pairwise comparison remained significant after FDR correction. title: Hepatitis aguda de patrón hepatocelular asociada a infección primaria por virus de Epstein-Barr en una mujer inmunocompetente: reporte de caso
abstract: Introducción: La afectación hepática asociada a infección aguda por virus de Epstein-Barr es frecuente, aunque generalmente cursa con elevaciones leves y autolimitadas de las aminotransferasas. La hepatitis aguda clínicamente manifiesta como forma predominante de presentación constituye una manifestación menos habitual y puede representar un reto diagnóstico. Presentación del caso: Mujer de 25 años, inmunocompetente, con antecedente de hipotiroidismo primario y síndrome ovárico metabólico poliendócrino, quien presentó síndrome febril de 12 días de evolución asociado a dolor en hipocondrio derecho. Durante su evaluación se documentó leucocitosis con linfocitosis absoluta marcada, hepatoesplenomegalia y elevación significativa de aminotransferasas con patrón predominantemente hepatocelular (AST 417 U/L, ALT 833 U/L), bilirrubinas normales y función sintética hepática conservada. Inicialmente se consideraron diversas etiologías infecciosas y hepatobiliares; sin embargo, la presencia de hepatoesplenomegalia y linfocitosis orientó la sospecha hacia infección por VEB. Los estudios serológicos mostraron anticuerpos anti-VCA IgM y anti-VCA IgG positivos, con EBNA negativo, compatibles con infección aguda por VEB. Se descartaron infección por VIH, hepatitis B y hepatitis C. La tomografía abdominal evidenció hepatomegalia y esplenomegalia sin datos de obstrucción biliar. La paciente recibió tratamiento de soporte, con evolución clínica favorable y descenso progresivo de las alteraciones hematológicas y bioquímicas durante la hospitalización y el seguimiento ambulatorio. Conclusiones: La infección aguda por VEB debe considerarse dentro del diagnóstico diferencial de pacientes jóvenes con síndrome febril, hepatoesplenomegalia, linfocitosis y hepatitis aguda, incluso en ausencia de las manifestaciones clásicas de mononucleosis infecciosa. El reconocimiento oportuno de esta entidad puede contribuir a orientar adecuadamente el abordaje diagnóstico diferencial.

title: Eligibility Criteria in Oncology Trials, 2000–2025: A Full-Census Classification Study With Policy Evaluation and Patient-Impact Conversion
abstract: Restrictive eligibility criteria limit accrual and generalisability of oncology trials. ASCO and Friends of Cancer Research issued broadening recommendations in 2017, and the US FDA issued final eligibility guidances in 2020, but whether restrictions actually changed has been studied only in single diseases, single items, or short periods. In this study we will classify the eligibility criteria of all interventional oncology trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov with start dates in 2000–2025 (frame defined by a prespecified condition term set; frozen snapshot of 91,014 records pulled 2026-11-18) on ten prespecified items: upper age limit, brain/CNS metastases, prior or concurrent malignancy, HIV, hepatitis B/C, organ function, performance status, cardiovascular disease, autoimmune disease, and psychiatric illness/substance abuse. Classification uses two independent non-generative decision models (Jev, TypeSafe AI, jev-1.13.0; Gemini Decisions, Google, gemini-decision-1) answering identical typed questions; records on which both models agree at probability ≥0.9 form the agreement zone. A two-part validation sample of 800 records (500 random, era-stratified; 300 enriched for discordant and rare-label records) will be labelled independently by two blinded human adjudicators, with blinded third adjudication of non-converging records, to estimate per-item sensitivity, positive predictive value, and specificity of the pipeline. Primary analyses are annual restriction prevalence and an interrupted time series at 2017 and 2020 for the five guidance-targeted items, under a prespecified contrast hypothesis (targeted items change; non-targeted items do not, or worsen). A secondary ecological analysis converts the distribution of upper age limits into the estimated share of incident patients potentially excluded by age limits alone, using US Cancer Statistics age distributions, with the Japanese National Cancer Registry as a sensitivity population.

title: Anomalía de Ebstein: diagnóstico tardío en un adulto con cirrosis hepática de etiología multifactorial: Ebstein's anomaly: Late diagnosis in an adult with multifactorial liver cirrhosis
abstract: Introduction: Ebstein's anomaly (EA) is a rare congenital heart disease (<1 %), characterized by apical displacement of the tricuspid valve, resulting in severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Its presentation in the fourth decade of life is exceptional. Case report: A 41-year-old male with a history of HBV/HCV infection, intravenous substance use, and tricuspid endocarditis in 2009, was admitted due to refractory ascites, anasarca, and progressive dyspnea. Imaging studies revealed massive TR due to previously undiagnosed EA, portal hypertension due to multifactorial cirrhosis (congestive, viral, and toxic), and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF). Discussion: EA, silent for decades, decompensated upon the appearance of PAF and sepsis. Cirrhosis is not exclusively viral/toxic; chronic venous congestion due to severe TR significantly contributed to liver damage (congestive hepatopathy), evidenced by a VExUS grade III score and disproportionate cholestasis. Management of PAF posed a dilemma: although CHA2DS2-VASc 2 indicates anticoagulation, bleeding risk due to esophageal varices in Child-Pugh C (HAS-BLED 2) contraindicates it, opting for rate control with carvedilol, which also reduces portal pressure. Conclusion: EA should be considered in the differential diagnosis of unexplained right heart failure in young adults. In every patient with chronic liver disease showing an atypical or diuretic-refractory course, systematic echocardiographic evaluation is indicated to rule out an underlying congestive cardiac cause. Management requires a multidisciplinary approach (cardiology, gastroenterology, infectious diseases).

title: Temporal dissection of hepatitis C virus and orthoflavivirus infections by continuous luminescence monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT Virus infection is a dynamic process consisting of rapidly evolving viral and host events, yet conventional endpoint assays provide only fragmented snapshots of these processes. Here, we established a unified temporal framework for dissecting virus–host interactions by integrating continuous bioluminescence monitoring with molecular and functional analyses. Real-time monitoring of hepatitis C virus (HCV) single-round infectious particles (SRIPs) revealed a biphasic replication profile consisting of an initial transient phase, followed by replication-dependent amplification. This transition was independently validated by similar HCV RNA kinetics observed after infection with HCV SRIPs or fully infectious HCV. Extension of this approach to dengue, Zika, and yellow fever virus SRIPs demonstrated that infection kinetics are determined by virus-specific replication programs and are modulated by the combination of viral replicons/capsids and prM/E proteins. This temporal framework enabled the identification of virus–host interactions that are difficult to resolve by conventional endpoint analyses. Early-phase cytoplasmic proteomics, combined with functional screening, identified the dynein light chain component DYNLRB2 as a previously unrecognized negative regulator of early HCV infection. Continuous monitoring also distinguished phase-specific antiviral activities, revealing distinct kinetic inhibition profiles for daclatasvir, acetylsalicylic acid, and interferon-α. Furthermore, delayed activation of the ER stress sensor ATF6 was first detected 40–47 h after HCV infection, and transcriptomic analysis at reporter-defined time points characterized the accompanying transition in host gene expression. Together, our study establishes continuous temporal monitoring as a general strategy for resolving dynamic virus–host interactions and for uncovering molecular events that remain obscured by conventional endpoint analyses. IMPORTANCE Viral infection is a dynamic process in which entry, genome amplification, host-factor requirements, antiviral effects, and cellular responses occur on different timescales. Conventional endpoint assays can identify changes in these processes but provide limited information about when they emerge or transition from one stage to another. Here, we show that continuous monitoring, when combined with direct molecular and functional measurements, can place these otherwise separate observations within a common temporal framework. Using HCV and related orthoflavivirus SRIPs, we resolved early and replication-associated phases, identified host factors with stage-dependent effects, and distinguished profiles of antiviral inhibition. We further showed that ATF6-mediated ER stress activation emerged later than early HCV infection and viral RNA amplification. Thus, continuous temporal monitoring provides a general strategy for resolving dynamic virus–host interactions by defining the temporal relationships among viral processes, pharmacological effects, and host responses that remain obscured by conventional endpoint analyses.

source_records.abstract: ABSTRACT Virus infection is a dynamic process consisting of rapidly evolving viral and host events, yet conventional endpoint assays provide only fragmented snapshots of these processes. Here, we established a unified temporal framework for dissecting virus–host interactions by integrating continuous bioluminescence monitoring with molecular and functional analyses. Real-time monitoring of hepatitis C virus (HCV) single-round infectious particles (SRIPs) revealed a biphasic replication profile consisting of an initial transient phase, followed by replication-dependent amplification. This transition was independently validated by similar HCV RNA kinetics observed after infection with HCV SRIPs or fully infectious HCV. Extension of this approach to dengue, Zika, and yellow fever virus SRIPs demonstrated that infection kinetics are determined by virus-specific replication programs and are modulated by the combination of viral replicons/capsids and prM/E proteins. This temporal framework enabled the identification of virus–host interactions that are difficult to resolve by conventional endpoint analyses. Early-phase cytoplasmic proteomics, combined with functional screening, identified the dynein light chain component DYNLRB2 as a previously unrecognized negative regulator of early HCV infection. Continuous monitoring also distinguished phase-specific antiviral activities, revealing distinct kinetic inhibition profiles for daclatasvir, acetylsalicylic acid, and interferon-α. Furthermore, delayed activation of the ER stress sensor ATF6 was first detected 40–47 h after HCV infection, and transcriptomic analysis at reporter-defined time points characterized the accompanying transition in host gene expression. Together, our study establishes continuous temporal monitoring as a general strategy for resolving dynamic virus–host interactions and for uncovering molecular events that remain obscured by conventional endpoint analyses. IMPORTANCE Viral infection is a dynamic process in which entry, genome amplification, host-factor requirements, antiviral effects, and cellular responses occur on different timescales. Conventional endpoint assays can identify changes in these processes but provide limited information about when they emerge or transition from one stage to another. Here, we show that continuous monitoring, when combined with direct molecular and functional measurements, can place these otherwise separate observations within a common temporal framework. Using HCV and related orthoflavivirus SRIPs, we resolved early and replication-associated phases, identified host factors with stage-dependent effects, and distinguished profiles of antiviral inhibition. We further showed that ATF6-mediated ER stress activation emerged later than early HCV infection and viral RNA amplification. Thus, continuous temporal monitoring provides a general strategy for resolving dynamic virus–host interactions by defining the temporal relationships among viral processes, pharmacological effects, and host responses that remain obscured by conventional endpoint analyses.

title: Hepatitis C in Children and Adolescents: State of the Art
abstract: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection is an important cause of chronic liver disease in children and adolescents, despite its often asymptomatic and indolent course. In infants and children, infection is mainly acquired through vertical transmission, while horizontal transmission becomes increasingly relevant during adolescence. The introduction of direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) has revolutionised HCV management, providing highly effective and well-tolerated treatments. Current international guidelines recommend treatment for all children and adolescents aged ≥ 3 years with chronic HCV infection, preferably with pangenotypic, ribavirin-free regimens. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and sofosbuvir/velpatasvir are the main first-line options. Sofosbuvir plus daclatasvir represents an additional World Health Organization-recommended option, particularly in resource-limited settings. Despite these advances, early diagnosis, treatment adherence, and equitable access to DAAs remain essential to achieve HCV elimination in children.

title: ĐÁNH GIÁ KẾT QUẢ ĐIỀU TRỊ BẰNG THUỐC TDF TRONG 5 NĂM, TRÊN BỆNH NHÂN VIÊM GAN VIRUS B MẠN TÍNH (2020 -2025)
abstract: Mục tiêu: Để đánh giá hiệu quả dài hạn của thuốc TDF, uống 300mg/ngày, trong bệnh viêm gan virus B mạn tính, chúng tôi tiến hành nghiên cứu hồi cứu 180 bệnh nhân đang điều trị tại Phòng khám Ngoại trú Bệnh viện A – Thái Nguyên, giai đoạn 2020 – 2025. Kết quả: Trong 5 năm, các biểu hiện lâm sàng, gồm cả dịch ổ bụng, ổn định dần, nhưng 03 bệnh nhân xơ gan trước điều trị vẫn tồn tại gan to, lách to. Sau 3 năm điều trị, 100% tải lượng HBV-DNA về dưới ngưỡng (thời gian trung bình là 3,62 ± 1,53 tháng), chỉ số đông máu, albumin và bilirubin ổn định tốt. Tình trạng xơ hóa gan/xơ gan và chuyển đổi huyết thanh HBeAg đang cải thiện. Không ghi nhận tình trạng bùng phát virus và các biến chứng (trên siêu âm và AFP). Tuy nhiên, tình trạng thiếu máu, giảm số lượng tiểu cầu không thuyên giảm, tỷ lệ bệnh nhân có enzyme ALT trên ngưỡng dao động từ 23,1 - 40,3%, có 2 trường hợp suy thận nhẹ (01 trường hợp trước điều trị) và 02 trường hợp có loãng xương. Kết luận: Thuốc TDF có hiệu quả ức chế virus, cải thiện chức năng đông máu, chuyển hóa của gan và hồi phục tình trạng xơ hóa gan. Cần theo dõi tình trạng thiếu máu, chức năng thận, loãng xương và hiệu quả lâu dài của TDF.

title: A Rare Case of ABO-Incompatible Living Donor Liver Transplant in Hyperacute Liver
abstract: Hepatitis A virus (HAV) infection is usually self-limiting; however, acute liver failure (ALF) is a rare, life- threatening complication that may require emergency liver transplantation. When no ABO-compatible donor is available, ABO-incompatible living donor liver transplantation (ABOi-LDLT) may be the only option. However, preformed anti-donor antibodies increase the risk of antibody-mediated rejection, and conventional desensitisation may not be feasible when transplantation cannot be delayed. We report the case of a previously healthy 26-year-old man (blood group O positive) with HAV-related ALF who presented with grade IV hepatic encephalopathy, prothrombin time (international normalised ratio [INR]) 5.64, serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase (SGPT) 4615 U/L, lactate 12 mmol/L, and pH 7.2 (King's College Criteria [KCC] positive). He required intubation, mechanical ventilation, and continuous renal replacement therapy with haemoadsorption. As no compatible donor was available, emergency ABOi-LDLT was performed within 24 hours of admission using a right-lobe graft from his B-positive mother. Preoperative plasma exchange reduced anti-B IgG and IgM titres from 1:128 and 1:64 to 1:16 and 1:4, respectively. Intraoperative splenectomy and rituximab administration in two divided doses (intraoperatively and on postoperative Day 5), along with corticosteroids, triple immunosuppression, and serial antibody titre monitoring, were employed as part of the individualised desensitisation strategy. The postoperative course was complicated by ventilator-associated pneumonia due to carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, which was treated according to culture sensitivity, with temporary withholding of mycophenolate mofetil. A subsequent rise in antibody titres without associated graft dysfunction was managed successfully with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), highlighting the importance of antibody surveillance and tailored postoperative management. The patient was weaned from mechanical ventilation and discharged on postoperative Day 17 with stable graft function and no evidence of rejection. This case demonstrates that emergency ABOi-LDLT may be feasible in selected patients with rapidly progressive ALF when an ABO-compatible donor is unavailable, provided that individualised antibody reduction, close serological monitoring, and vigilant postoperative critical care are available.

However, preformed anti-donor antibodies increase the risk of antibody-mediated rejection, and conventional desensitisation may not be feasible when transplantation cannot be delayed. We report the case of a previously healthy 26-year-old man (blood group O positive) with HAV-related ALF who presented with grade IV hepatic encephalopathy, prothrombin time (international normalised ratio [INR]) 5.64, serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase (SGPT) 4615 U/L, lactate 12 mmol/L, and pH 7.2 (King's College Criteria [KCC] positive). He required intubation, mechanical ventilation, and continuous renal replacement therapy with haemoadsorption. As no compatible donor was available, emergency ABOi-LDLT was performed within 24 hours of admission using a right-lobe graft from his B-positive mother. Preoperative plasma exchange reduced anti-B IgG and IgM titres from 1:128 and 1:64 to 1:16 and 1:4, respectively. Intraoperative splenectomy and rituximab administration in two divided doses (intraoperatively and on postoperative Day 5), along with corticosteroids, triple immunosuppression, and serial antibody titre monitoring, were employed as part of the individualised desensitisation strategy. The postoperative course was complicated by ventilator-associated pneumonia due to carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, which was treated according to culture sensitivity, with temporary withholding of mycophenolate mofetil. A subsequent rise in antibody titres without associated graft dysfunction was managed successfully with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), highlighting the importance of antibody surveillance and tailored postoperative management. The patient was weaned from mechanical ventilation and discharged on postoperative Day 17 with stable graft function and no evidence of rejection. This case demonstrates that emergency ABOi-LDLT may be feasible in selected patients with rapidly progressive ALF when an ABO-compatible donor is unavailable, provided that individualised antibody reduction, close serological monitoring, and vigilant postoperative critical care are available.

title: Longitudinal fibrosis-4 monitoring: A promising approach for hepatocellular carcinoma risk stratification in treatment-naïve chronic hepatitis C
abstract: A substantial proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis C virus infection remain untreated worldwide, sustaining a cumulative and age-dependent risk of hepatocellular carcinoma, particularly in resource-limited settings. Conventional risk stratification relies on baseline “snapshots” of fibrosis stage and single-time-point biomarkers, which may fail to capture the dynamic biology of fibrogenesis and carcinogenesis. In a long-term retrospective cohort of treatment-naïve patients with chronic hepatitis C virus published in the World Journal of Gastrointestinal Oncology , Li et al reported that a 3-year increase in the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index (ΔFIB-4 ≥ 1.0) independently predicted subsequent hepatocellular carcinoma (adjusted hazard ratio approximately 2.7), with the increasing trajectory group exhibiting a high long-term cumulative incidence. These findings suggest that longitudinal biomarker trajectories may refine long-term risk stratification beyond baseline staging, although the timing and actionable thresholds require prospective validation. Biologically, progressive increases in FIB-4 may reflect ongoing extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammation-driven microenvironmental shifts, and vascular alterations that promote tumor development. However, interpretation must account for age-related score drift, biological variability, and nonhepatic confounding. We propose a pragmatic framework integrating threshold-crossing and slope-based monitoring, combining serial FIB-4 with alpha-fetoprotein and key demographic modifiers. High-risk longitudinal patterns may warrant the use of confirmatory elastography and the consideration of intensified surveillance, pending prospective validation. Prospective studies are needed to standardize longitudinal cutoffs and validate clinical implementation.

title: Detection of Hepatitis D Virus Antigen and RNA in Cutaneous Tissue from a Patient with HDV-Related Cirrhosis and Cutaneous Vasculitis
abstract: The presence of hepatitis D virus (HDV) in extrahepatic tissues has been rarely documented, and its potential contribution to systemic manifestations remains poorly understood. Here, we report a patient with HDV-related cirrhosis who developed cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis and underwent skin biopsy. Immunohistochemical analysis using two independent monoclonal antibodies directed against hepatitis delta antigen (HDAg) demonstrated HDV-specific staining in the epidermis, particularly in the spinous and granular layers. HDV RNA was also detected in skin biopsy specimens by quantitative real-time PCR. The concordance between HDAg detection and HDV RNA identification supports the presence of HDV components within the sampled cutaneous tissue. Following initiation of bulevirtide therapy, serum HDV RNA decreased and the patient’s vasculitis-related symptoms resolved. Although the detection of HDAg and HDV RNA does not demonstrate productive viral replication in the skin or establish a causal relationship between HDV and cutaneous vasculitis, these findings raise the possibility that HDV components may be detectable in extrahepatic tissues and warrant further investigation.

title: Clinical outcomes and laboratory correlates of documented liver failure among children hospitalized with hepatitis A at a tertiary referral hospital in Mogadishu, Somalia
abstract: Background Contemporary data on severe pediatric hepatitis A in Somalia are limited. This study describes clinical characteristics, documented liver failure, and in-hospital outcomes among hospitalized pediatric patients. Methods We conducted a hospital-based retrospective cohort study using FONET electronic health records and aggregate hospital screening statistics from 1 January 2020 to 31 December 2025. All included children had a positive serum immunoglobulin M antibody to hepatitis A virus (IgM anti-HAV) result verified in the laboratory section during the index admission. Documented liver failure was defined by the binary clinical diagnosis recorded in FONET and was analyzed without retrospective reclassification. Clinical-record review confirmed no pre-existing chronic liver disease; however, response of coagulopathy to parenteral vitamin K was unavailable, preventing independent adjudication of pediatric acute liver failure. Non-parametric comparisons and parsimonious logistic regression were used. Results From 1 January 2020 to 31 December 2025, 78,132 pediatric admission episodes were recorded, and 1,024 children were evaluated for suspected acute hepatitis. Of these, 691 were excluded (not identified as acute hepatitis A) after clinical and laboratory evaluation, leaving 333 serum IgM anti-HAV-positive records corresponding to 330 unique patient identifiers. After removing of one exact duplicate record and excluding 2 patients with unresolved discrepant duplicate records, a final sample of 328 children was included in the analysis. The median age was 4.0 (2.0–7.0) years, and 185 (56.4%) were boys. Documented liver failure occurred in 76 patients [23.2%; 95% confidence interval (CI), 18.9%–28.0%], hepatic encephalopathy was recorded in 31 of 325 children (9.5%), and 23 patients died (7.0%; 95% CI, 4.7%–10.3%). Each doubling of total bilirubin was associated with higher odds of documented liver failure [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 1.46; 95% CI, 1.18–1.81], whereas higher albumin was associated with lower odds (aOR per 1 g/dL, 0.31; 95% CI, 0.19–0.50). Higher albumin was also associated with lower in-hospital mortality (aOR, 0.21; 95% CI, 0.10–0.42). Conclusions Documented liver failure and in-hospital mortality represented substantial clinical burdens in this hospitalized cohort. Total bilirubin and albumin were independently associated with documented liver failure, whereas albumin was associated with mortality. These findings represent clinical associations rather than a validated prediction model.

title: Membranoproliferative Glomerulonephritis Associated With Renal Schistosomiasis in a Young Patient From Chad: A Report of a Rare Case
abstract: We report the case of a 17-year-old male patient from a rural area who was initially followed in a paediatric setting and subsequently referred to the Nephrology Department for corticosteroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome. The patient had a history of frequent freshwater exposure and tested positive for hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibodies. Clinical evaluation and paraclinical investigations revealed nephrotic syndrome characterised by severe proteinuria (+++), hypoalbuminemia (19.9 g/L), and generalised oedema, complicated by macroscopic haematuria (++) and impaired renal function. Renal biopsy demonstrated lobular membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN) with extracapillary proliferation, moderate chronic tubulointerstitial nephropathy, and focal renal schistosomiasis. The clinical outcome was favourable following two courses of the antiparasitic drug praziquantel combined with corticosteroid therapy, resulting in parasite eradication, recovery of renal function, and return to normal daily activities.

title: Manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, estudios transversales y retrospectivos. Resultados: la exposición ocupacional a la sangre, sobre todo por objetos punzocortantes, fue el principal riesgo para el personal. La vacunación contra la hepatitis B y la profilaxis posexposición fueron las medidas más eficaces frente a las infecciones sanguíneas. Frente al SARS-CoV-2 se recomendaron el triaje, el control de aerosoles y el equipo de protección. Conclusión: el manejo se basa en precauciones estándar aplicadas a todos los pacientes, que permiten una atención segura y sin discriminación.

title_original: Predicting hepatitis B virus DNA elevation during pregnancy: Toward risk-stratified monitoring beyond the traditional viral-load threshold

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of traditional viral-load thresholds in predicting hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA elevation during pregnancy, highlighting the need for improved risk-stratified monitoring to better manage maternal and fetal health.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a retrospective analysis conducted in Ethiopia, focusing on maternal HBV DNA levels and their association with elevation during mid-to-late pregnancy. It involved a moderate-sized dataset and did not include external validation.
analysis.methods: The researchers developed a model using maternal age and baseline HBV DNA levels ≥ 100 international units per milliliter to predict DNA elevation during pregnancy. The model was based on existing data and did not involve prospective testing or external validation.
analysis.main_results: Maternal age and baseline HBV DNA ≥ 100 international units per milliliter were found to predict mid-to-late pregnancy elevation. However, the model could not predict transmission, maternal flares, or treatment needs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as a step toward risk-stratified monitoring, suggesting that dynamic surveillance could improve timely antiviral prophylaxis and reduce mother-to-child transmission. This approach is novel in its focus on predictive modeling beyond traditional viral-load thresholds.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform more targeted antenatal surveillance strategies for HBV-infected pregnant women, potentially improving outcomes by enabling earlier interventions and reducing the risk of mother-to-child transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's retrospective design, lack of external validation, and moderate performance limit its applicability for clinical decision-making. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the use of predictive modeling to identify factors associated with hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA elevation during pregnancy, aiming to move beyond traditional viral-load thresholds. The authors found that maternal age and baseline HBV DNA levels ≥ 100 international units per milliliter could predict elevation in mid-to-late pregnancy. However, the model cannot predict transmission, maternal flares, or treatment needs. The study's retrospective design and lack of external validation limit its strength, though the findings suggest a potential for improved risk-stratified monitoring. These results may inform more targeted antenatal surveillance strategies for HBV-infected pregnant women, potentially enhancing outcomes by enabling earlier interventions and reducing mother-to-child transmission risks.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决传统病毒载量阈值在预测妊娠期间 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) DNA 升高方面的局限性,强调需要改进风险分层监测,以更好地管理母婴健康。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是在埃塞俄比亚进行的一项回顾性分析,重点关注母亲 HBV DNA 水平及其与妊娠中晚期升高的关系。它涉及中等大小的数据集,不包括外部验证。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员开发了一个模型,使用母亲年龄和基线 HBV DNA 水平≥100国际单位/毫升来预测怀孕期间 DNA 升高。该模型基于现有数据,不涉及前瞻性测试或外部验证。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,母亲年龄和基线 HBV DNA ≥ 100 国际单位/毫升可以预测中晚期妊娠升高。然而,该模型无法预测 传播、产妇突发或 治疗 需求。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为迈向风险分层监测的一步,表明动态 监测 可以改善及时的 传播 预防并减少母婴 传播。这种方法的新颖之处在于它专注于超越传统病毒载量阈值的预测模型。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为感染 HBV 的孕妇提供更有针对性的产前 监测 策略,通过早期干预和降低母婴 传播 风险可能改善结局。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的回顾性设计、缺乏外部验证以及中等的性能限制了其在临床决策中的适用性。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决传统病毒载量阈值在预测妊娠期间 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) DNA 升高方面的局限性,强调需要改进风险分层监测,以更好地管理母婴健康。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是在埃塞俄比亚进行的一项回顾性分析,重点关注母亲 HBV DNA 水平及其与妊娠中晚期升高的关系。它涉及中等大小的数据集,不包括外部验证。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员开发了一个模型,使用母亲年龄和基线 HBV DNA 水平≥100国际单位/毫升来预测怀孕期间 DNA 升高。该模型基于现有数据,不涉及前瞻性测试或外部验证。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究发现,母亲年龄和基线 HBV DNA ≥ 100 国际单位/毫升可以预测中晚期妊娠升高。然而,该模型无法预测 传播、产妇突发或 治疗 需求。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为迈向风险分层监测的一步,表明动态 监测 可以改善及时的 传播 预防并减少母婴 传播。这种方法的新颖之处在于它专注于超越传统病毒载量阈值的预测模型。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为感染 HBV 的孕妇提供更有针对性的产前 监测 策略,通过早期干预和降低母婴 传播 风险可能改善结局。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的回顾性设计、缺乏外部验证以及中等的性能限制了其在临床决策中的适用性。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

full_text: Vol. 18(1), pp. 20-27, July-December 2026 DOI: 10.5897/IJGMB2026.0237 Article Number: B16831675133 ISSN 2006-9863 Copyright©2026 Author(s) retain the copyright of this article http://www.academicjournals.org/IJGMB International Journal of Genetics and Molecular Biology Full Length Research Paper Prevalence of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) in Côte d'Ivoire Jacques Renaud Dechi*, Aya Jeanne Armand Ake, Saydou Kabore, Jean-Louis Philippe N'Din, Salimata Moussa, Doris Oura, Bamory Dembele, Liliane Siransy and Yassongui Mamadou Sekongo Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS), National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d'Ivoire (CNTSCI), Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire. Received 3 August, 2026; Accepted 13 October, 2026 Chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection exacerbates hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease. In Côte d’Ivoire, HDV is systematic not systematically screened among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)- positive blood donors, and most regional estimates rely on anti-HDV serology, which indicates exposure but not active replication. This study aimed to determine HDV RNA replication positivity among HBsAg- positive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d’Ivoire (CNTSCI), using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). A cross-sectional study based on a non-probability convenience sample was conducted in March 2021. HDV RNA was detected by nested RT-PCR targeting two genomic regions (nucleotides 888–1122 and 313–485). Of 51 donors included, 75% were male (n = 38) and and mean age was 37 ± 9 years. HBV DNA results were available for 43 donors (84%). Among them, HDV RNA positivity was 88.9% (32/36) in those with detectable HBV viraemia and 100% (7/7) in those with undetectable viral load, giving an overall positivity 90.7% (39/43). This figure applies only to donors with available viral load data not the entire cohort of 51 donors. HDV RNA was also detected in donors receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with suppressed HBV viraemia. Given the convenience sample of donors already in follow-up care, findings are hypothesis-generating rather than population-level estimates. These results support larger representative studies and systematic HDV screening during follow-up of individuals with chronic HBV infection. Key words: Hepatitis B virus/hepatitis delta virus (HBV/HDV) co-infection, nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), molecular epidemiology, convenience sample, transfusion medicine, West Africa. INTRODUCTION Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains one of the most widespread infectious agents worldwide. An estimated 254 million people were living with chronic HBV infection in 2022, resulting in approximately 1.1 million deaths, while only 13% of carriers had been diagnosed and 3% had received treatment (World Health Organization [WHO], 2024). Sub-Saharan Africa bears a disproportionate share of this burden, with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) prevalence exceeding 8% in many areas and estimated at 9 to 12% among the general adult population in Côte d’Ivoire (WHO, 2021). A meta-analysis involving more than 3.5 million African blood donors reported a pooled HBsAg seroprevalence of 10.09% in West Africa, the highest among the continent’s five regions (Quintas et al., 2024). This substantial burden is consistent with findings indicating that HBsAg prevalence among blood donors at the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d’Ivoire (CNTSCI) remained stable over two decades (Seri et al., 2018). Hepatitis delta virus (HDV), first described by Rizzetto in 1977 (Rizzetto et al., 1980), is a defective RNA virus that depends on HBV surface antigen for its replication and transmission. Consequently, HDV infection occurs only in HBsAg-positive individuals, either through simultaneous HBV/HDV coinfection or through HDV superinfection in individuals with pre-existing chronic HBV infection. Approximately 90% of individuals with chronic HBV infection who acquire HDV superinfection progress to chronic HDV infection, whereas simultaneous HBV/HDV coinfection is usually resolved, although serological markers may persist without ongoing viral replication (Rizzetto et al., 2021). This distinction is important when comparing anti-HDV antibody prevalence, which indicates previous or current exposure, with HDV RNA positivity, which provides evidence of active viral replication. HBV/HDV coinfection is associated with more severe liver disease than HBV monoinfection, increasing the risk of cirrhosis by approximately two- to three-fold and the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma by approximately two-fold. Cirrhosis may develop in 70 to 80% of affected patients within 5 to 10 years (Fattovich et al., 2000; Negro, 2014; Noureddin and Gish, 2014). Globally, an estimated 15–20 million HBsAg-positive individuals are thought to have HDV infection, although these estimates may be inflated when subpopulation weighting is not adequately considered (Rizzetto, 2015; Polaris Observatory Collaborators, 2024). Data on HDV infection in sub-Saharan Africa remain limited and heterogeneous. Reported anti-HDV seroprevalence ranges from approximately 7% in pooled estimates for West Africa to more than 25% in Central Africa (Stockdale et al., 2017). Country-specific estimates also vary considerably, ranging from 1 to 54% in Cameroon (Besombes et al., 2020), 7 to 22% in Mauritania (Mansour et al., 2012; Lunel-Fabiani et al., 2013), and 8 to 9% in Nigeria (Opaleye et al., 2016). In Senegal, active HDV replication confirmed by RNA testing was detected in 61.5% of anti-HDV-seropositive individuals, despite an Dechi et al. 21 overall anti-HDV seroprevalence of only 1.5% (Wembulua et al., 2025). These findings illustrate the distinction between antibody-based estimates of exposure and RNA- based evidence of active infection. Before the present study, published data on HBV/HDV coinfection in Côte d’Ivoire were very limited. Regarding treatment, pegylated interferon had long remained the principal therapeutic option, despite its limited efficacy (Wedemeyer et al., 2011). The approval of bulevirtide by the European Medicines Agency introduced a new treatment option for chronic HDV infection (Asselah et al., 2020), although access remains limited in resource-constrained settings. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of active HDV RNA replication among HBsAg-positive blood donors receiving follow-up care at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the CNTSCI, using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) targeting two distinct HDV genomic regions. The secondary objectives were to describe the sociodemographic and virological characteristics of this population and examine the relationship between HDV RNA positivity and HBV viraemia. MATERIALS AND METHODS Study setting and design This was a cross-sectional, descriptive and analytical study conducted in March 2021 at the CNTSCI, specifically within the CMSDS. Laboratory analyses were performed at the molecular biology platform of the Immunology Laboratory of the UFR of Medical Sciences (UFR-SM) at Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny. Study population, sampling strategy and inclusion criteria The target population consisted of voluntary blood donors regularly followed at the CMSDS with confirmed positive HBsAg serology. Recruitment used a non-probabilistic, exhaustive convenience sampling strategy: all HBsAg-positive donors attending scheduled CMSDS follow-up visits during the study period and satisfying the inclusion criteria were consecutively invited to participate. Inclusion criteria were: (i) being a voluntary blood donor followed at the CMSDS; (ii) presenting a confirmed positive HBsAg result; and (iii) having provided consent to participate in the study. Donors whose biological samples were insufficient or of poor quality were excluded. Collection and pre-treatment of biological samples Blood samples were collected from each participant in Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) tubes. Viral RNA extraction A preliminary centrifugation step of 1 mL of aliquoted plasma at 14,000 rpm for 1 hour at 4°C yielded a pellet enriched in viral particles, which served as the starting template for HDV RNA extraction. Extraction was performed using the QIAamp Viral RNA Mini Kit (Qiagen, Germany) according to the manufacturer's instructions. Extracts were stored at −80°C. The extraction protocol comprised the following successive steps: viral lysis, nucleic acid precipitation, RNA capture on a silica column, washing, and RNA elution. Viral lysis: 140 μL of the plasma pellet was added to 560 μL of AVL buffer containing carrier RNA. The mixture was vortexed for 15 s and then incubated for 10 min at room temperature. Precipitation and capture: After the addition of 560 μL of absolute ethanol and centrifugation, the lysate was transferred onto a QIAamp silica membrane column for selective binding of nucleic acids. Two successive washes (AW1 and AW2 buffers) removed contaminants. Final elution was performed with 60 μL of molecular-biology-grade water. An exogenous RNA internal control was added to each sample to monitor extraction efficiency, reverse transcription, and PCR inhibition. Received 3 August, 2026; Accepted 13 October, 2026 Chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection exacerbates hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease. In Côte d’Ivoire, HDV is systematic not systematically screened among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)- positive blood donors, and most regional estimates rely on anti-HDV serology, which indicates exposure but not active replication. This study aimed to determine HDV RNA replication positivity among HBsAg- positive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d’Ivoire (CNTSCI), using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). A cross-sectional study based on a non-probability convenience sample was conducted in March 2021. HDV RNA was detected by nested RT-PCR targeting two genomic regions (nucleotides 888–1122 and 313–485). Of 51 donors included, 75% were male (n = 38) and and mean age was 37 ± 9 years. HBV DNA results were available for 43 donors (84%). Among them, HDV RNA positivity was 88.9% (32/36) in those with detectable HBV viraemia and 100% (7/7) in those with undetectable viral load, giving an overall positivity 90.7% (39/43). This figure applies only to donors with available viral load data not the entire cohort of 51 donors. HDV RNA was also detected in donors receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with suppressed HBV viraemia. Given the convenience sample of donors already in follow-up care, findings are hypothesis-generating rather than population-level estimates. These results support larger representative studies and systematic HDV screening during follow-up of individuals with chronic HBV infection. Key words: Hepatitis B virus/hepatitis delta virus (HBV/HDV) co-infection, nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), molecular epidemiology, convenience sample, transfusion medicine, West Africa. INTRODUCTION Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains one of the most widespread infectious agents worldwide. An estimated 254 million people were living with chronic HBV infection in 2022, resulting in approximately 1.1 million deaths, while only 13% of carriers had been diagnosed and 3% had received treatment (World Health Organization [WHO], 2024). Sub-Saharan Africa bears a disproportionate share of this burden, with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) prevalence exceeding 8% in many areas and estimated at 9 to 12% among the general adult population in Côte d’Ivoire (WHO, 2021). A meta-analysis involving more than 3.5 million African blood donors reported a pooled HBsAg seroprevalence of 10.09% in West Africa, the highest among the continent’s five regions (Quintas et al., 2024). This substantial burden is consistent with findings indicating that HBsAg prevalence among blood donors at the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d’Ivoire (CNTSCI) remained stable over two decades (Seri et al., 2018). Hepatitis delta virus (HDV), first described by Rizzetto in 1977 (Rizzetto et al., 1980), is a defective RNA virus that depends on HBV surface antigen for its replication and transmission. Consequently, HDV infection occurs only in HBsAg-positive individuals, either through simultaneous HBV/HDV coinfection or through HDV superinfection in individuals with pre-existing chronic HBV infection. Approximately 90% of individuals with chronic HBV infection who acquire HDV superinfection progress to chronic HDV infection, whereas simultaneous HBV/HDV coinfection is usually resolved, although serological markers may persist without ongoing viral replication (Rizzetto et al., 2021). This distinction is important when comparing anti-HDV antibody prevalence, which indicates previous or current exposure, with HDV RNA positivity, which provides evidence of active viral replication. HBV/HDV coinfection is associated with more severe liver disease than HBV monoinfection, increasing the risk of cirrhosis by approximately two- to three-fold and the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma by approximately two-fold. Cirrhosis may develop in 70 to 80% of affected patients within 5 to 10 years (Fattovich et al., 2000; Negro, 2014; Noureddin and Gish, 2014). Globally, an estimated 15–20 million HBsAg-positive individuals are thought to have HDV infection, although these estimates may be inflated when subpopulation weighting is not adequately considered (Rizzetto, 2015; Polaris Observatory Collaborators, 2024). Data on HDV infection in sub-Saharan Africa remain limited and heterogeneous. Reported anti-HDV seroprevalence ranges from approximately 7% in pooled estimates for West Africa to more than 25% in Central Africa (Stockdale et al., 2017). Country-specific estimates also vary considerably, ranging from 1 to 54% in Cameroon (Besombes et al., 2020), 7 to 22% in Mauritania (Mansour et al., 2012; Lunel-Fabiani et al., 2013), and 8 to 9% in Nigeria (Opaleye et al., 2016). In Senegal, active HDV replication confirmed by RNA testing was detected in 61.5% of anti-HDV-seropositive individuals, despite an Dechi et al. 21 overall anti-HDV seroprevalence of only 1.5% (Wembulua et al., 2025). These findings illustrate the distinction between antibody-based estimates of exposure and RNA- based evidence of active infection. Before the present study, published data on HBV/HDV coinfection in Côte d’Ivoire were very limited. Regarding treatment, pegylated interferon had long remained the principal therapeutic option, despite its limited efficacy (Wedemeyer et al., 2011). The approval of bulevirtide by the European Medicines Agency introduced a new treatment option for chronic HDV infection (Asselah et al., 2020), although access remains limited in resource-constrained settings. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of active HDV RNA replication among HBsAg-positive blood donors receiving follow-up care at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the CNTSCI, using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) targeting two distinct HDV genomic regions. The secondary objectives were to describe the sociodemographic and virological characteristics of this population and examine the relationship between HDV RNA positivity and HBV viraemia. MATERIALS AND METHODS Study setting and design This was a cross-sectional, descriptive and analytical study conducted in March 2021 at the CNTSCI, specifically within the CMSDS. Laboratory analyses were performed at the molecular biology platform of the Immunology Laboratory of the UFR of Medical Sciences (UFR-SM) at Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny. Study population, sampling strategy and inclusion criteria The target population consisted of voluntary blood donors regularly followed at the CMSDS with confirmed positive HBsAg serology. Recruitment used a non-probabilistic, exhaustive convenience sampling strategy: all HBsAg-positive donors attending scheduled CMSDS follow-up visits during the study period and satisfying the inclusion criteria were consecutively invited to participate. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) RNA replication among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive blood donors in Côte d'Ivoire. A cross-sectional design was used, with a convenience sample of 51 donors, of whom 75% were male and the mean age was 37 ± 9 years. HDV RNA was detected using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) targeting two genomic regions. Among 43 donors with HBV DNA results, 88.9% had detectable HDV RNA in those with HBV viraemia, and 100% had HDV RNA positivity in those with undetectable HBV viral load, resulting in an overall positivity of 90.7%. These results suggest a high prevalence of HDV co-infection among HBV-positive individuals and support the need for systematic HDV screening in follow-up care. However, the findings are hypothesis-generating due to the convenience sample used.

abstract_zh: 慢性丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 感染会加剧 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 相关肝病。在科特迪瓦,未对乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 阳性献血者进行系统性筛查,大多数区域估计依赖于抗 HDV 血清学,这表明暴露但不活跃复制。本研究旨在确定 HBsAg 阳性献血者中 HDV RNA 复制阳性情况。科特迪瓦国家输血中心 (CNTSCI) 的献血者医疗随访中心 (CMSDS) 使用巢式逆转录聚合酶链式反应 (RT-PCR)。2021 年 3 月进行了一项基于非概率便利样本的横断面研究。通过针对两个基因组区域(核苷酸 888-1122 和 313-485)的巢式 RT-PCR 检测了 HDV RNA。51 名捐献者中其中,75% 为男性 (n = 38),平均年龄为 37 ± 9 岁。43 名捐献者 (84%) 可获得 HBV DNA 结果。其中,可检测到 HBV 病毒血症的 HDV RNA 阳性率为 88.9% (32/36),病毒载量无法检测到的患者为 100% (7/7),总体阳性率为 90.7% (39/43)。该数字仅适用于具有可用病毒载量数据的捐献者,而不是 51 名捐献者的全部 队列研究。在接受富马酸替诺福韦二吡呋酯 (TDF) 且 HBV 病毒血症受到抑制的捐献者中也检测到 HDV RNA。考虑到已经处于后续护理中的捐献者的方便样本,研究结果是假设生成而不是人群水平估计。这些结果支持更大规模的代表性研究和个体随访期间的系统性 HDV 筛查关键词:乙型肝炎病毒/丁型肝炎病毒(HBV/HDV)合并感染,巢式逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR),分子流行病学,方便样本,输血医学,西非。

title: Semi-quantitative ultrasound scoring reveals hepatic structural recovery and immune modulation during tenofovir alafenamide therapy in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system, and to investigate the correlation between sonographic changes and immune function restoration. Methods A total of 100 CHB patients who received TAF monotherapy (25 mg/day) for at least 24 months were retrospectively enrolled. A seven-parameter semi-quantitative US score, encompassing liver echogenicity, capsular contour, margin shape, vessel clarity, portal vein diameter (PVD), spleen thickness (ST), and splenic vein velocity (SVV), was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Concurrently, serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), peripheral T-cell subsets, including cluster of differentiation 3-positive (CD3 + ), CD4 + , CD8 + T cells, CD4+/CD8+ ratio, and natural killer (NK) cell activity were measured. Correlations between US scores and biochemical/immune parameters were analyzed. Results At 24 months, all patients achieved HBV DNA <20 IU/mL, with ALT and AST normalization rates of 92% and 95%, respectively. The comprehensive US score decreased significantly from 7.86 ± 1.73 at baseline to 3.37 ± 0.95 at 24 months ( P < 0.001), with the most pronounced improvements observed in capsular smoothness and parenchymal homogeneity. The CD4 + T-cell proportion and CD4 + /CD8 + ratio increased, whereas the CD8 + proportion decreased; NK cell activity rose from 42.7 ± 7.3% to 52.4 ± 6.2% ( P < 0.05). The US score was positively correlated with ALT (r = 0.56) and AST (r = 0.47), and negatively correlated with the CD4 + /CD8 + ratio (r = −0.46) and NK cell activity (r = −0.38) (all P < 0.01). Conclusion These findings indicate that TAF not only suppresses viral replication and normalises liver enzymes but also promotes measurable structural liver improvement, as reflected by declining semi-quantitative US scores. The strong correlations of US scores with biochemical and immune parameters support its utility as a non-invasive imaging biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system. It aimed to assess the correlation between sonographic changes and immune function restoration. A total of 100 CHB patients on TAF monotherapy for at least 24 months were enrolled. The US score, which included seven parameters, was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Serum HBV DNA, ALT, AST, and immune parameters were also measured. At 24 months, all patients achieved HBV DNA <20 IU/mL, with ALT and AST normalization rates of 92% and 95%, respectively. The US score significantly decreased, indicating structural liver improvement. The US score correlated positively with ALT and AST and negatively with CD4+/CD8+ ratio and NK cell activity. The strong correlations support the use of US as a non-invasive biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of reported limitations.

title_zh: 半定量超声评分揭示慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)在接受替诺福韦艾拉酚胺治疗期间肝脏结构恢复和免疫调节
source_body_en: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system, and to investigate the correlation between sonographic changes and immune function restoration. Methods A total of 100 CHB patients who received TAF monotherapy (25 mg/day) for at least 24 months were retrospectively enrolled. A seven-parameter semi-quantitative US score, encompassing liver echogenicity, capsular contour, margin shape, vessel clarity, portal vein diameter (PVD), spleen thickness (ST), and splenic vein velocity (SVV), was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Concurrently, serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), peripheral T-cell subsets, including cluster of differentiation 3-positive (CD3 + ), CD4 + , CD8 + T cells, CD4+/CD8+ ratio, and natural killer (NK) cell activity were measured. Correlations between US scores and biochemical/immune parameters were analyzed. Results At 24 months, all patients achieved HBV DNA <20 IU/mL, with ALT and AST normalization rates of 92% and 95%, respectively. The comprehensive US score decreased significantly from 7.86 ± 1.73 at baseline to 3.37 ± 0.95 at 24 months ( P < 0.001), with the most pronounced improvements observed in capsular smoothness and parenchymal homogeneity. The CD4 + T-cell proportion and CD4 + /CD8 + ratio increased, whereas the CD8 + proportion decreased; NK cell activity rose from 42.7 ± 7.3% to 52.4 ± 6.2% ( P < 0.05). The US score was positively correlated with ALT (r = 0.56) and AST (r = 0.47), and negatively correlated with the CD4 + /CD8 + ratio (r = −0.46) and NK cell activity (r = −0.38) (all P < 0.01). Conclusion These findings indicate that TAF not only suppresses viral replication and normalises liver enzymes but also promotes measurable structural liver improvement, as reflected by declining semi-quantitative US scores. The strong correlations of US scores with biochemical and immune parameters support its utility as a non-invasive imaging biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在利用半定量超声(US)评分系统评估替诺福韦艾拉酚胺二甲基磺酸盐(TAF)在慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)患者中的治疗反应,并探讨超声影像变化与免疫功能恢复之间的相关性。方法 入选了100例接受TAF单药治疗(25 mg/天)至少24个月的慢性乙型肝炎患者进行回顾性分析。在基线、12个月和24个月时计算了包含肝脏回声、包膜轮廓、边缘形态、血管清晰度、门静脉直径(PVD)、脾脏厚度(ST)和脾静脉血流速度(SVV)的七参数半定量超声评分。同时测量了血清乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)脱氧核糖核酸(DNA)、丙氨酸氨基转移酶(ALT)、天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶(AST)以及外周T细胞亚群,包括分化簇3阳性(CD3+)、CD4+、CD8+ T细胞、CD4+/CD8+比值和自然杀伤(NK)细胞活性。分析了超声评分与生化和免疫参数之间的相关性。结果 在24个月时,所有患者均达到HBV DNA <20 IU/mL,ALT和AST的正常化率分别为92%和95%。综合超声评分从基线的7.86 ± 1.73显著下降至24个月的3.37 ± 0.95(P < 0.001),其中包膜平滑度和实质均匀性的改善最为显著。CD4+ T细胞比例和CD4+/CD8+比值增加,而CD8+ T细胞比例下降;NK细胞活性从42.7 ± 7.3%上升至52.4 ± 6.2%(P < 0.05)。超声评分与ALT(r = 0.56)和AST(r = 0.47)呈正相关,与CD4+/CD8+比值(r = −0.46)和NK细胞活性(r = −0.38)呈负相关(所有P < 0.01)。结论 这些发现表明,TAF不仅抑制病毒复制并使肝酶正常化,还促进可测量的肝脏结构改善,这体现在半定量超声评分的下降。超声评分与生化和免疫参数之间的强相关性支持其作为非侵入性影像生物标志物用于监测治疗疗效和肝脏修复的潜力。
